answer: The velvet design assumes the worst: one operator pretending to be a crowd, and prices admission accordingly. Admission is priced by congestion: when joins spike, the fee climbs automatically, cooling the rush. Under the island, a farm cannot sneak a thousand clones in at the quiet price — its own volume pushes the price up with every identity it registers. That is the point of the willow: cloning stops paying the moment each copy costs as much as the original.
